subject: Private deployment: platform fee amortization and SRE credit timing
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@helioshealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: Jamie Tan <jamie.tan@helioshealth.com>, procurement@helioshealth.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify fees for private VPC pilot -> prod

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed by the latency profile. Before we take this to procurement/legal I need one thing clarified: how does Redwood expect the platform fee and SRE retainer to be billed for a 6-month pilot that transitions into production? Specifically:

- Can the platform fee be amortized across the pilot and production commitments, or is it invoiced up-front?
- Do SRE retainer credits (for onboarding and runbook handover) apply against the first invoice or are they posted as a one-time credit after go-live?

We want to avoid a big up-front hit during the pilot. Attached our standard procurement checklist (Helios_SOW_v1.pdf). Please point us to the exact invoicing cadence and any conditions that trigger credit delivery.

Best,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, Helios Health
From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@helioshealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Mar 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify fees for private VPC pilot -> prod

Alex — great question and totally reasonable. TL;DR: we can structure the commercials to avoid a large pilot upfront payment while protecting our implementation costs. Details below and a proposed invoice schedule at the end.

Platform fee treatment:
- Standard: platform fee is a timebound annualized fee; by default we invoice 50% at contract signature and 50% at go-live.
- Pilot-friendly option (recommended for Helios): invoice 25% at signature (covers staging and minimal capacity), 25% at pilot go-live (measured by agreed smoke tests), and the remaining 50% amortized over the first 6 months of production invoices (monthly). This reduces upfront cashflow pressure.

SRE/onboarding credits:
- Onboarding SRE retainer (8 weeks) is typically issued as a credit line on the first invoice after go-live.
- We can make an exception: issue a provisional credit note (equal to estimated SRE hours) applied to the pilot invoice, with final reconciliation after production cutover. That way Helios sees immediate relief.

Conditions & triggers:
- Pilot go-live defined by test plan signoff (Annex A) and one week of stable telemetry (errors <0.5% and latency SLA met for 95th pct).
- Final amortization kicks in once a production PO is raised for the agreed committed capacity.

Proposed invoice schedule (example for a 12-month agreement with 6-month pilot -> prod):
- Day 0 (signature): 25% platform fee invoice
- Pilot go-live: 25% platform fee invoice minus provisional SRE credit (if accepted)
- Month 1..6 production: monthly platform amortization invoices (remaining 50% split across 6 months) + metered usage charges

Attachments: I’m attaching a worked example (Redwood_TCO_v2.xlsx) that maps to the numbers above.

Let me know if this aligns with procurement expectations and whether you prefer the provisional-credit approach for SRE. If yes, I’ll have Legal draft a short amendment to the SOW.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify fees for private VPC pilot -> prod

Quick internal note: pricing ops + legal will want a cap on the provisional credit exposure. Recommend we cap provisional SRE credit at the lesser of estimated hours or $45k, with reconciliation at production PO. Also suggest we require a signed pilot acceptance form (one page) to avoid disputes about the "stable telemetry" clause.

If procurement pushes for 0 upfront, we should push back — implementation work has real cost. The 25%/25%/amortize model is defensible and easier for accounting.

Marissa
VP, Commercial Deals — Redwood Inference
From: Jamie Tan <jamie.tan@helioshealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@helioshealth.com>, procurement@helioshealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2025 11:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify fees for private VPC pilot -> prod

Thanks — that schedule looks workable. A couple of follow-ups from my side (legal/procurement):

1) Procurement needs exact invoice language for the amortized platform fee (we typically require installment schedule in Exhibit B of the SOW). Can you provide a one-paragraph clause we can drop into the SOW?
2) For the provisional SRE credit: procurement will accept it if Redwood includes a reconciliation clause and a cap (please provide the cap amount and reconciliation timeline).
3) PO timing: Helios prefers to issue a master PO that covers pilot and the first three months of production, then renew/extend with a second PO once production usage is stable. Will Redwood accept that?

If we can get those three items clarified, procurement is green to proceed to signature next week.

Jamie Tan
Senior Counsel, Helios Health
From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: Jamie Tan <jamie.tan@helioshealth.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@helioshealth.com>, procurement@helioshealth.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify fees for private VPC pilot -> prod

Jamie — appreciate the clear asks. Below are the exact items you can drop into Exhibits and SOW. I’ll also instruct SalesOps to generate a one-pager installment exhibit and share a DocuSign link by EOD.

1) Installment clause (one paragraph for Exhibit B):
"The Platform Fee shall be invoiced in installments as follows: 25% upon execution of this Agreement, 25% upon completion of the Pilot Go-Live Acceptance as defined in Annex A, and the remaining 50% to be amortized in equal monthly installments over the first six (6) months of Production. Production commences upon Customer issuance of a Production Purchase Order referencing this Agreement."

2) Provisional SRE credit (cap & reconciliation):
"Redwood will issue a provisional SRE credit to Customer in the amount of USD 45,000 applied against the invoice issued at Pilot Go-Live. Redwood and Customer will reconcile actual SRE hours within thirty (30) days following Production Cutover. Any difference in the estimated versus actual SRE effort will be invoiced or credited within the following invoice cycle."

3) PO timing acceptance: Redwood accepts Customer issuance of a master PO that covers Pilot and the first three (3) months of Production provided that the PO references the applicable Exhibit and the Production Purchase Order trigger described above.

Next steps (from Redwood):
- I will ask SalesOps to create Exhibit B with the installment schedule and attach the provisional credit clause to Annex A.
- Generate DocuSign package (SOW + Exhibit B + Annex A) and send to Jamie/procurement for signature.
- SalesOps will mark provisional credit as limited exposure in our billing system and tag DEAL-4832.

If that wording is acceptable, please confirm and we’ll route the DocuSign today.

Best,
Priyom
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_TCO_v2.xlsx (worked example), Helios_SOW_v1.pdf (procurement checklist)
